cells.location: KURNOOL DISTRICT / PATTIKONDA TALUK — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place:
Daḍḍādi-Kōṭakoṇḍa.—From Shri K.
Nallareddi, through Shri H. V. Sarma.
cells.remarks: Records that the regions around Yādavadurga and Drōṇā- chala having become deserted, the king proclaimed the settlement and offered that the people should go and settle there and that in response to this, people from Guddili, Billakalu, Bāyala, Mānukōṭi, etc., approached the king and secured the right of the settlement for Daḍḍi-Kōṭakoṇḍa which was one of the regions thrown open for settlement. Appears to be spurious, since the king mentioned in this record ruled about 100 years later.

cells.date: Śaka 1304, (yuga-vigad-anala-ni śā-karo), Dundubhi, Chaitra śu. 1, lunar eclipse Saturday, = 1382 A.D., March 29.
cells.remarks: Records that when the king's first son (kumāra-agraja) Bukka (II) was ruling from Penukoṇḍa (Pṛthula-śallapuri), his minister Vāsudēva, son of Sēllarāya of the Ātrēya-gōtra, requested the king to grant the same to his lord as Bukkasāyapuram and allotted the same to a number of Brāhmaṇas. It is also stated that Sēllarāya caused the construction of a tank through his son. Both the village and the tank were situated on the western side of the village Āroviḍu.

cells.place: Plates from Shri M. K. Dhavalikar, Kaikāya New Delhi.
cells.remarks: Issued from Vijayakāndivīpa. Records the grant, by the ruler, of a grove (ārāma) and pukkiti, (i.e., certain kinds of lands) to the village Mahājanas, a corporate community of 'Buddhist monks' during the reign of a certain Ravi-mahārāja. Jina-ānandi-sēnāpati, son of Sinha-sēnāpati, figures as the writer of the charter. In characters of about 7th century A.D. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXVII, pp. 29-30 and Plate.

cells.location: Madras
cells.place: Plates in the Government Museum. Findspot: Not known. Impressions through Shri P. R. Srinivasan. Set No. 1.
cells.remarks: Records the reconstitution into a manaiyitu, the agrahāra constituted earlier by the Chōḷa king, described as Virāḍi-vīraṇ Vīrāṇḍaguḍaiyān in Kali 4187, Śaka 1008, Nandana, Vaikāśi, 22, for the upkeep of the temple of the deity, Tiruvēṅkaṭa-nāmichāri. It is stated that the Rāyar had a tank also there. It is also stated that Kōṭṭaiyān paid 250 pon for the purpose. The seal at the top of the plate bears a legend in Telugu characters. The plate is written in a script of Tamil in Telugu reading Yekkōl Appāji. In modern characters. Noticed in the Cut. of C.P. grants in the Govt. Museum, Madras, Chōḷas, No. 4, p. 15.

cells.remarks: The first plate is broken and damaged. Records the royal grant of the village Utapālaka situated near Dattabhaṭṭ-ānaka in the province of Surāshṭra for the purposes of the worship of the Buddha in the temple constructed by the merchant (vaṇijaka) Kumikāla and situated within the Duḍḍā-vihāra. cells.place: Bhōi.—Plate in the possession of Bala-gauḍa Śivagauḍa Pāṭil. Through Dr. B. R. Gopal.
cells.remarks: This spurious record, in characters of the 10th century, registers a royal gift of the village Ammaṇikā along with the villages Būḍagāḷige, Muguḷikoḍu, Bennevaḍa and Eṇḍegoḍu situated in Koṇḍanūr-viṣaya, free from taxes, to Chāvuṇḍa-chatur-vēdi-bhaṭṭa of the Kausika-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Hārīta gōtra respectively. The gift was made at the request of the chief queen, by the king from his Vijaya-skandhāvāra at Banavāsi. He is stated to have been the son of Simhavarman and grandson of Śarvavarman. Mahā sandhivigrahī Guṇavarman wrote the record. Noticed in Progress of Kannada Research in Bombay State (1947-52), pp. 17-18.

cells.place: No. 5.
cells.remarks: Registers an endowment of 250 dhārā-gaḍyāṇa to the bhaṇḍāra of god Kṛishṇadēva of Uḍupi, worshipped by the religious heads of the aṣṭa-saṃsthāna who were the followers of the sampradāya of Śrīmad-Ānandatīrtha-āchārya. The gift was made, on the recommendation of the chief of Mysore, son of Bhadrayya and grandson of Vīraṇayya of Gautama-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Ṛik-śākha, for per-forming the worship of the god on Madhva-navamī day and also daily for the maintenance of the lamp, etc., worth 12 varāha per annum. The details of the services to the god on this day are enumerated. The endowment was made during the period of Raghuvaryatīrtha-śrīpāda who was then in charge of the worship of the god.

Records the gift of lands in the village Māvaṇḍūr alias Rājaśēkhara-Karpūrapuram as dēvabhōga by Bommu-nāyaka, the ruler of Vēlūr, for conducting the daily worship and services to the deity Sōmanāthadēva, for the merit of his father Nāgama-nāyakkar-aiyan. It is said that the above village, situated on the north side of the Kuṉṟavardhana-kōṭṭam, a division in Paḍavīḍu rājya included in the Jayankoṇḍaśōla-maṇḍalam, was purchased by the donor from the mahājanas of the village and granted. Paḍavīḍu is described as the rājadhānī of Āraṇi-rājya. The donor is described as the son of Nāgama and the grandson of Tippu-nāyaka.

The land was purchased by him for the purpose of burning a lamp for Virumādēvi-īśvaramuḍaiyār, the Mahādēva of the village. The sabhā is stated to have received some money from him towards the price of the land and the tax-exemption granted.

cells.date: Śaka 1139, Īśvara, Pushya ba. 10, Monday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti = 1217 A.D., December 25.
cells.remarks: Commences with the obeisance, Om namaḥ-paramaśivāya etc., of Siddhārāma. Records that Mahāpradhāna Saṅgamadēva-Nāyaka, accompanied by the Mahājanas, Jayasiṅgadēva, . . . . dēva, Gaṅgādēva, Parigidēva and Śambhūdēva, renamed the village of Attinūru as Liṅgāpura and made a gift of the village Ittage, situated in Amkulage-80 & hamlet of Attinūru, to the god Kapilasiddha-Mallikārjuna of Sonnalige. cells.remarks: Fragments. One fragment refers to the installation of an image of a deity and the construction of a temple at Kūḍalūr in Kōṇḍaśōḷa-maṇḍalam. cells.location: GOA Tisvadi Taluk Velhā Goa — Goa
cells.place: Cathedral of Francis of Assisi. Loose slabs in the compound.
cells.remarks: Records a royal order prohibiting the evil practice of nīpīrūk prevalent in the mosque at Guwā (Goa), by which the property of some persons, e.g. a house, a shop, a garden, a slave, etc., but no son, was confiscated to the state with the result that the above-mentioned relations were put to great hardship. The order seems to have been issued following the representation by Malik-ush Sharq Malik Zāhid Beg to the nā’ib-i-ghāibat of the ma’āmala and was conveyed to the desā’is, the muqaddams, the khūts (khots) and also to the head collectors (beldar) of the region and of the island of Goa. The order further enjoins upon the men of Kokan (i.e. Konkan) region to refrain from accusing one another.

Bar. State, Vol. I, p. 16 and A. R. Ep., 1961-62, No. C 1311.

cells.remarks: States that from old times, the ta'ziya rites in the Janambara of Banjipura were performed by the forefathers of Chand, son of Banjipura Khan, Himmat Khan and Raja Khan and that for ensuring the continuance of the old practice it was decided at the time of (name illegible) that the family yearly amount (fixed by?) the gadi of the gadi in the faujdari will be utilised for the said purpose. cells.place: East side of the biggest tower
cells.date: A. H. 1166, Rabī' II 12, Friday-1753 A.D., February 16.
cells.remarks: Do. Language and execution crude. Records the construction of the tower in eleven stages (?) in the dargāh of Qādir Walī. The construction of the tower (minār) was carried out by the orders of the ruler. Also refers to the foundation of the Qādir-Penth near Tuḷjā-Mahārāj. Further mentions Mānojī Rāō, the sar-khel, Tanōjī Rāō Bhōnsle, Marāṭhā, and the name of the Ḥākim, the amīn (?). Genealogy of the ruler wrongly given in reverse order as: 'Umdat-ul-Mulk Rājā Mahārāj Ekojī Rājā, Tuḷjā, Sijī or Pratāp Singh. For the Marāṭhī portion, see Appendix B, No. 292.

cells.remarks: Trilingual. Badly damaged and composition faulty. Contains the text of a royal farmān granting the village Janja(?) along with lands, gardens, etc., to the mosque at Kolhapur, given formerly in the jāgīr of Fachhād Khān as reward(?) to Khān-i-A'zam Nūr Khān for his services in suppressing the revolt of Bījāpūr. For the Marathi and Kannada portions, see Appendix B, No. 330.

cells.place: No. 4. Do.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Contains the text of a farmān, issued by the king ‘Ādil Shāhī, laying down conditions in respect of a well and garden in mauḍa Sirol in pargana Rāybāg given in in‘ām to a saint. It also lays down a system of taxes upon the needy people, and forbidding any person or descendants of the said Khān to make money out of it or alter it and not to refuse fruits and vegetables grown in the land to mendicants or to raise the rates. Cf. ibid., p. 35. Cf. ibid., p. 80. For the Marathi portion, see Appendix B, No. 332.

cells.place: Loose slab on the brink of a ruined stop- well in Pīr-kā-Maḷa.
cells.remarks: Records the text of a maḥḍar (decision by assembly) made by the maḥājans and balōṭiyās (village officials) of the qaṣba Hukkēri to the effect that the house of Jai Sethi (?) situated in the vicinity of the guest-house, endowed the fountain (kāraṇya) and the guest-house (mihmān-khāna) constructed for public use by Mangūr Khān (see No. 245 above) for the benefit of the travellers and the poor, one-third and one-fourth for the guest-house. It also states that the land was given to the custody of Mīrān, son of Ḥasan. Also quotes in full the names of the persons attending the maḥḍar. In late characters of about the 16th or early 17th century. Cf. A.R.Ep., 1942-43, B.K. No. 4.

cells.location: Koṭla
cells.place: On the entrance gateway of a mosque.
cells.remarks: States that the foundation of this mosque was laid on the first date during the reign of Muḥammad Shāh, son of Fīrūz Shāh (Tughluq). It is further stated that the building materials of the temple in the mauḍa Sainthali, where Hindus used to assemble in large numbers every year and which was destroyed by the Khān on the representation of the qāḍī of the place, were used for the mosque. The inscription gives second date by Khān-i-A‘ẓam Khānzāda Ḥātim Khān and the dome of the entrance was built by Malik Qamar-i-Dīn under the superintendence of Muṣṭafā b. Dīn sar-kār-i-jāgīr-i-dīwān. Cf. Khwāja ‘Azīz. Cf. ibid., Vol. XX, pp. 131 32, plate XXXI.
